title: Review: The Game Store Report
setup:
import pandas as pd
sales = pd.read_csv("sales.csv")
players = pd.read_csv("players.csv")
games = pd.read_csv("games.csv")
explanation: Level 4 review! Three tables are ready: sales (who bought which game, and when), players and games. Each sale only stores IDs: player_id says who bought it and game_id says which game. You can chain merges: sales.merge(players, on="player_id").merge(games, on="game_id"). Use everything from Level 4: merging, join types, dates and charts.

lines.explain: Add the buyer's details to each sale.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: how many rows does this have? (sales has 13 rows.)
hints: Every sale matches exactly one game.

solution_lines.explain: Each of the 13 sales finds its game: 13 rows.

tasks.prompt: Show how much each player spent in total (username and total), rounded to 2 decimals, biggest spender first.
hints: Chain both merges, then groupby username, sum price, round and sort.

solution_lines.explain: Sales with player and game details.

tasks.prompt: Draw a bar chart of the number of sales per year.
hints: Convert the dates first, then group by year and count, then plot.

tasks.prompt: Find the players who never bought a game. Show just username.
hints: Left join players to sales, then look for missing sale_id (Lesson 20).
m = players.merge(sales, on="player_id", how="left"), then m[m["sale_id"].isna()][["username"]]

solution_lines.explain: Players with no sale: speedy_g and mochi.

tasks.prompt: Show the total money spent per player country, rounded to 2 decimals, biggest first.
hints: Same chain as task 2, but group by country.

solution_lines.explain: Spending per country: the USA leads.

recap: Level 4 complete! You can combine tables (merge, concat), work with dates, and turn results into charts. That's a full analysis workflow.
